interest: Japanese naval use of Taiwan for southern expansion.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.33, File 1046) contains diplomatic despatches, military intelligence cablegrams, and consular reports from July 1933 to September 1938 monitoring the movements, exercises, and forward deployment of the Imperial Japanese Navy across East and Southeast Asia. The collection opens with an exhaustive account of the 1933 visit to Taiwan by the Japanese Combined Fleet and three royal prince-officers, providing detailed orders of battle and public declarations by Japanese admirals identifying Taiwan as their front line of defense against the United States. Subsequent documents include a 1934 U.S. Army intelligence cable outlining massive fleet maneuvers simulating simultaneous defense against Pacific and Malayan naval thrusts, confidential eyewitness reporting by an American consul of secret fleet and submarine maneuvers at Keelung in 1935, observations of a foreign cadet training cruise at Singapore in 1937, and a 1938 report on Japanese naval incursions near French Indochina following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese War. Together, these records chronicle the steady militarization of Japan's southern periphery and the growing alarm among Western powers as Japanese naval operations edged toward Southeast Asia.

subfiles.about: Reports on the visit of three imperial princes serving in the Japanese Navy and the arrival of the Combined Fleet in Taiwan.
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Taihoku, Taiwan
subfiles.summary: Consul Ketcham details the extensive visit of the Imperial Japanese Allied Fleet, composed of the First and Second Squadrons under Admirals Kobayashi and Suyetsugu, to Keelung, Mako, and Takao. Three imperial princes serving as naval officers—Prince Kuni, Prince Takamatsu, and Prince Fushimi—accompanied the fleet and toured various inland and southern cities amidst stringent security measures prompted by a 1928 assassination attempt in Taichu. Ketcham provides a complete list of capital ships, destroyers, and submarines participating in the cruise. In addition, the despatch records press statements by the commanding admirals emphasizing Taiwan's critical role as Japan's southern defensive outpost and alluding to strained relations with the United States.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Ketcham (Taihoku) on Visit of Royal Princes and Imperial Japanese Fleet to Taiwan
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo, Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits military intelligence regarding Japanese naval and army maneuver concentrations scheduled in southern Formosa.

subfiles.title: Confidential Despatch from Palmer (Saigon) on Japanese Naval Activities near French Indochina
